# Matthew Goff

Professor of Religion

Distinguished Research Professor

* * *

![Image 2: Dr. Matthew Goff](https://religion.fsu.edu/sites/default/files/2024-08/Matthew-Goff-3x2.jpg)

## Contact Information

[mgoff@fsu.edu](mailto:mgoff@fsu.edu)

415/417 Diffenbaugh

Office Hours

By appointment only

## About

Matthew Goff joined the faculty of the Department of Religion in 2005. He completed an M.T.S degree in 1997 at Harvard Divinity School and finished his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago in 2002. Goff studied under John Collins and wrote a dissertation on a Qumran text entitled 4QInstruction. His publications focus on the Dead Sea Scrolls and ancient Judaism. His most recent book is "The Apocrypha: A Guide" (Oxford, 2024). Goff's current book project is on demons and monsters in ancient Judaism and early Christianity.

Program Area

Religions of Western Antiquity

Keywords

Apocalypticism, The Dead Sea Scrolls, Second Temple Judaism

Publications

*   “The Expansive Wisdom of a Great Sage: Is There a Book of Ben Sira in Rabbinic Literature?” in T _eaching and Learning the Norms of Life and Faith: Pedagogues, Educators and their Heritage in Abrahamic Religions_(ed. Catalin-Stefan Popa; Seraphim; Tübingen: Mohr Siebeck, 2025), 15-41.
*   [“Odd Conspiracies: John Allegro, Sacred Mushrooms, and the Dead Sea Scrolls.”](https://www.mdpi.com/2077-1444/16/8/946 "“Odd Conspiracies: John Allegro, Sacred Mushrooms, and the Dead Sea Scrolls.”")_Religions_ 16 (2025) (special issue, “On the Origins of Western Psychedelia: Exploring Allegro’s _The Sacred Mushroom and the Cross_”).
*   “All in the Family: The Book of Tobit, the Legend of Ahiqar, and the Cultural Politics of Kinship in the Hellenistic Age,” in _Missing Pieces: Essays in Honour of Eibert J.C. Tigchelaar_(ed. Arjen F. Bakker et al.; STDJ 152; Leiden: Brill, 2025), 218-41.
*   With Jens Wilkens. “Enoch the Buddha King: The Nachleben of Enochic Traditions in Central Asia.” _Gnosis_ 10 (2025): 209-42 (thematic issue on Judaism and Manichaeism).

Position Type

Faculty

# **Religions Across Borders**

Florida State University's Department of Religion is a vibrant hub of intellectual inquiry and exploration. It fosters an environment where students and scholars delve into the rich tapestry of religious traditions from around the world, emphasizing the historical, social, philosophical, ethical, and ritual aspects of various religions.

[More About Religion](https://religion.fsu.edu/about)

![Image 2: Rebecca Peters conducting research.](https://religion.fsu.edu/sites/g/files/upcbnu446/files/2024-06/RebeccaPeters.jpg)

## **High-Level Research**

As one of the first state universities in the nation to offer graduate study in religion, the department still plays a leading role in training top tier scholars in religion. With four tracks of study, scholars are given the opportunity to hone in on their research area and expand their education through additional symposiums and lectures offered.

[Explore Graduate Program](https://religion.fsu.edu/graduate)

![Image 3: Janeen Green, undergraduate student in the Department of Religion.](https://religion.fsu.edu/sites/g/files/upcbnu446/files/2024-06/Janeen-Green-01-900x600.jpg)

## **Introductory Studies**

FSU offers one of the most comprehensive undergraduate religion majors in the country. Courses examine the array of religious cultures around the globe from historical, ethical, philosophical, cultural, and social perspectives. Students can study languages relevant to religious traditions, and they work alongside faculty on directed independent studies and honors theses.

[Explore Undergraduate Program](https://religion.fsu.edu/undergraduate)

# **Religions Across Borders**

Florida State University's Department of Religion is a vibrant hub of intellectual inquiry and exploration. It fosters an environment where students and scholars delve into the rich tapestry of religious traditions from around the world, emphasizing the historical, social, philosophical, ethical, and ritual aspects of various religions.

[More About Religion](https://religion.fsu.edu/about)

![Image 2: Rebecca Peters conducting research.](https://religion.fsu.edu/sites/g/files/upcbnu446/files/2024-06/RebeccaPeters.jpg)

## **High-Level Research**

As one of the first state universities in the nation to offer graduate study in religion, the department still plays a leading role in training top tier scholars in religion. With four tracks of study, scholars are given the opportunity to hone in on their research area and expand their education through additional symposiums and lectures offered.

[Explore Graduate Program](https://religion.fsu.edu/graduate)

![Image 3: Janeen Green, undergraduate student in the Department of Religion.](https://religion.fsu.edu/sites/g/files/upcbnu446/files/2024-06/Janeen-Green-01-900x600.jpg)

## **Introductory Studies**

FSU offers one of the most comprehensive undergraduate religion majors in the country. Courses examine the array of religious cultures around the globe from historical, ethical, philosophical, cultural, and social perspectives. Students can study languages relevant to religious traditions, and they work alongside faculty on directed independent studies and honors theses.

[Explore Undergraduate Program](https://religion.fsu.edu/undergraduate)
